title: The Drop of the Green Zone
premise: Wendell Ishikawa, a disgraced intelligence analyst haunted by a catastrophic misjudgment she can barely remember, is approached by a stranger named Ada Voss who claims Wendell once saved her life — a favor Wendell has no memory of doing. Ada's 'repayment' drags Wendell into a conspiracy: a staged industrial accident timed to the Green Zone summit, designed to kill hundreds and fracture a fragile peace accord. As Wendell races to decode the plot, she discovers her own erased memories are the key — and that the man who wiped them sits inside the summit's security detail. In the end, Wendell chooses found family over institutional loyalty, exposes the architect at the cost of Ada's sacrifice, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Casper Ishikawa is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent years adjacent to international summits before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose institutions fail them, drawing on a childhood split between Osaka and Portland.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Insomniac and blacklisted, Wendell works dead-end contract analysis until Ada Voss appears at her door claiming Wendell saved her in Jakarta — an event Wendell cannot recall. Ada leaves a burner phone and a warning: someone is watching Wendell too. The beat is uneasy curiosity: the first crack in Wendell's numb isolation.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The burner rings with intercepted chatter about a 'drop' scheduled during the Green Zone summit. Wendell verifies it against old agency patterns and realizes the signature matches work she did before her memory gap. She contacts Ada against every instinct. Emotional beat: reluctant re-engagement with a world that discarded her.

chapters.title: Green Zone Rules
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada reveals the plot: a gas main 'failure' engineered to collapse a summit hotel, laundered through three shell companies. She needs Wendell's pattern-recognition skills to find the operational cell. Their wary partnership forms over bad coffee and worse trust. Beat: two lonely women testing whether they can rely on each other.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, Zero Alibis
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell pulls strings to access her own sealed personnel file and finds redactions where the incident should be — someone inside scrubbed her memory of a prior summit warning she'd flagged. A tail follows her home; she loses them using tradecraft she didn't know she had. Beat: dread mixed with dawning competence.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wiped Me
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Surveillance identifies Deputy Security Director Marcus Hale as the architect — and as the man who ordered Wendell's memory suppression after she flagged the same vulnerability two years ago. Ada wants him exposed publicly; Wendell hesitates, terrified of what else is buried in her head. Beat: love-against-duty tension between the partners.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Under hypnosis from a sympathetic retired doctor, fragments return: Wendell once ran a safehouse, sheltering defectors — including a young Ada — and burned it to save them, erasing herself to survive the fallout. Beat: grief and self-forgiveness begin; the 'incident' was mercy, not failure.

chapters.title: Countdown at the Canal
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The team locates the device staging site at a canal warehouse but walks into a trap; Ada takes a bullet covering Wendell's escape. Wendell, now fully awake to what she's lost and found, refuses to run. Beat: found family crystallizes through blood and sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. With hours before the summit, Wendell goes alone to Hale under cover of returning to the fold, feeding him doctored analysis while Ada's surviving contacts trace the trigger signal. Hale suspects, tests her, nearly breaks her. Beat: peak tension — Wendell performing loyalty to the institution that destroyed her.

chapters.title: Accident, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Wendell and Ada's POV alternating. The climax: Wendell triggers the evacuation by faking a fire alarm cascade, forcing the plotters to abort or be caught; Ada, wounded but mobile, kills the remote trigger from a rooftop. Hale is arrested on live feeds he can't spin. Beat: catharsis — duty fulfilled on their own terms.

chapters.title: Sleep Through the Night
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Weeks later, official inquiries whitewash everything, but Wendell no longer needs their absolution. She and Ada, recovering, share a quiet apartment above a canal café; the burner phone rings with a new voice needing help, and Wendell answers willingly. Final beat: belonging earned, insomnia broken, found family chosen.
